# Validation: every solver against textbook cases

<!-- GENERATED by `node scripts/validation-report.mjs`. Do not edit: `npm run validation:check` fails when this file differs from a fresh run. -->

371 cases in 15 domains. 371 pass their tolerance.

Every number in the "measured" column was produced by running the solver, not typed. `node scripts/validation-report.mjs` runs each case in
[`validation/`](../validation) through the public API (the built `box3d-webgpu-kit` for the rigid world and its couplings, `src/engine` for the
other solvers) and writes this file, [`public/validation/validation.json`](../public/validation/validation.json) and the page served at
`<site>/validation/`. `npm run validation:check` runs in the pull-request gate and fails if a case misses its tolerance or if the committed
files no longer match a fresh run.

How to read a row:

- **Reference** is the closed-form answer, with the formula it comes from. Where the answer needs a number only the solver knows (a float32 mass), the reference uses that number.
- **Error** is measured minus reference: as a fraction of the reference (a percentage, or "rel." when it is below 0.01%) when the tolerance is relative, otherwise in the unit of the quantity.
- **Tolerance** is the one the linked test asserts for the same quantity (where a note says so, the one its document states). A case passes when the error is inside it.
- A convergence **order** is measured from two or three resolutions of the same problem: `log(e_coarse / e_fine) / log(ratio)`.
- Numbers are printed with 7 significant digits (errors with 3) and stored with 9. The check accepts a fresh value that differs from the committed one by less than
  1e-6 of the case's tolerance band or 5e-9 relative, whichever is larger, and treats two defects against zero as equal when both are under
  0.001 of their tolerance (that is round-off). On one build two runs give identical files.
- A pass means the solver reproduces that textbook case to that tolerance. It does not make a scene built with the solver an engineering prediction; the limits are listed under each domain.

## Rigid bodies, joints and shapes

Free fall, pendulums, friction, restitution, collisions, forces and torques, joint motors and springs, motion on triangle-mesh and height-field ground, compound bodies (summed mass, centre of mass and inertia, tipping, rest) and explicit mass data (stated mass, centre of mass and inertia tensor).

Solver: Box3D compiled to WebAssembly, through `box3d-webgpu-kit` (float32 state, 240 Hz, 4 sub-steps). 42 cases, 42 pass. Model and limits: [README.md](../packages/box3d-kit/README.md).

<details><summary>What each case measures, and the test that asserts it</summary>

- **Free fall: speed after 2 s** (`rigid.free-fall.speed`): speed of a falling sphere. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v08.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v08.test.mjs), "free fall follows y = h - g t^2 / 2 and mass is density x volume for each shape".
- **Free fall: height after 2 s** (`rigid.free-fall.height`): height of a sphere dropped from 100 m. Semi-implicit Euler falls g t dt / 2 further than the continuum answer; the tolerance is exactly that plus 1 mm. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v08.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v08.test.mjs), "free fall follows y = h - g t^2 / 2 and mass is density x volume for each shape".
- **Mass of a sphere** (`rigid.mass.sphere`): mass, density 1000 kg/m^3, r = 0.25 m. The world stores mass in float32. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v08.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v08.test.mjs), "free fall follows y = h - g t^2 / 2 and mass is density x volume for each shape".
- **Mass of a box** (`rigid.mass.box`): mass, density 2700 kg/m^3, 0.2 x 0.4 x 0.6 m. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v08.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v08.test.mjs), "free fall follows y = h - g t^2 / 2 and mass is density x volume for each shape".
- **Mass of a capsule** (`rigid.mass.capsule`): mass, density 500 kg/m^3, r = 0.3 m, half length 0.5 m. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v08.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v08.test.mjs), "free fall follows y = h - g t^2 / 2 and mass is density x volume for each shape".
- **Mass of a convex hull (octahedron)** (`rigid.mass.hull`): mass of the hull of six unit axis points, density 1000 kg/m^3. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v08.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v08.test.mjs), "convex hulls: mass is density x volume and a hull rests on its face".
- **A cube hull rests on the ground** (`rigid.hull.rest-height`): centre height of a 1 m cube hull at rest. Box3D lets resting contacts sink by its linear slop (5 mm). - **Compound pendulum: amplitude kept** (`rigid.pendulum.amplitude`): largest angle between 25 s and 30 s. - **Compound pendulum: hinge force** (`rigid.pendulum.hinge-force`): force carried by the hinge at the end of the run. - **Compound: tipping angle of the L** (`rigid.compound.tipping`): tilt of gravity at which the L turns over the edge of its base (bisected to 0.016 degrees, 8 s a run). Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs), "a compound resting on the ground stays at rest and goes to sleep".
- **Compound: no creep at rest** (`rigid.compound.rest-speed`): largest linear or angular speed of the L between 1 s and 6 s. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs), "a compound resting on the ground stays at rest and goes to sleep".
- **Explicit mass: F = m a** (`rigid.mass-data.force`): speed after 14 N acts for 1 s on a sphere told to weigh 7 kg (its shape says 4.19 kg). Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs), "explicit mass data: a body spins up at I^-1 torque, accelerates at F / m, and keeps the values across a type change".
- **Explicit inertia: tau = I alpha** (`rigid.mass-data.torque`): spin after 6 N m acts for 1 s about an axis told to have I = 3 kg m^2 (its shape says 0.017). Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs), "explicit mass data: a body spins up at I^-1 torque, accelerates at F / m, and keeps the values across a type change".
- **Explicit inertia: a full tensor couples the axes** (`rigid.mass-data.cross-coupling`): angular velocity about y after a torque of 0.3 N m about x acts for 0.05 s on a body with products of inertia. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs), "explicit mass data: a body spins up at I^-1 torque, accelerates at F / m, and keeps the values across a type change".
- **Explicit inertia: Euler's equations over 2 s** (`rigid.mass-data.euler`): relative difference of the body-axis angular velocity from an RK4 solution, full tensor, body-fixed torque, about 1.7 rad turned. The engine integrates the gyroscopic term implicitly with one Newton step per sub-step; the torque is re-aimed once a step. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs), "explicit mass data: a body spins up at I^-1 torque, accelerates at F / m, and keeps the values across a type change".
- **Explicit centre of mass: a pendulum from stated mass data** (`rigid.mass-data.centre-of-mass`): period of a sphere hinged through its centre and told that its centre of mass is 0.3 m below with I = 0.05 kg m^2, mean over 20 s. From its shape the body would not swing at all: the hinge passes through the sphere's centre. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs), "an explicit centre of mass: a hinged sphere swings with the period its stated mass data imply, and setting them keeps the motion".
- **Compound and mass data: replay** (`rigid.compound.replay`): a recording with compound bodies, setMassData and resetMassData, replayed from its JSON (0: every checkpoint and the final hash match). Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs), "recordings with compound bodies and mass data replay bit for bit, and a worker-hosted world agrees with a local one".

</details>

### What is not validated: rigid bodies, joints and shapes

- Stacks, piles and many-body contact: every case here has one or two bodies in contact. Stack stability and friction in piles are not checked against a reference.
- Rolling is checked for a sphere only, and the contact slips slightly (the rolling case allows 1%). There is no rolling-resistance or spinning-friction reference.
- Restitution is checked at one speed and one coefficient. Box3D applies restitution only above a threshold speed.
- Wheel, weld and spherical joints have no closed-form row here: wheel and weld joints are tested for behaviour only (a car drives and steers, a weld keeps its spacing).
- Compound bodies: a body holds at most 64 convex shapes (box, sphere, capsule, hull); overlapping shapes count their overlap twice in mass and inertia. Contact of a compound is checked at rest and at tipping only, not in stacks or impacts. Triangle meshes and height fields are static only and cannot be part of a compound.
- Explicit mass data replace the numbers, not the shapes: nothing checks that a stated tensor is physically possible for the collision shape (the triangle inequality of the principal moments is not required), and a body with partly locked rotation is not covered.
- One build on one machine. The cross-device determinism matrix is a separate roadmap item; the kit records identical hashes on arm64 Node and Bun only.

## Rigid bodies in water

Archimedes for three shapes, draught, volume and force balances, heave and roll periods, terminal velocity, the righting moment and the energy budget.

Solver: `box3d-webgpu-kit/coupling`: exact submerged volumes of boxes, spheres and capsules on a linear shallow-water basin (float64), two-way. 22 cases, 22 pass. Model and limits: [WATER_COUPLING.md](./WATER_COUPLING.md).

### What is not validated: rigid bodies in water

- One rectangular basin with a flat bottom and closed walls. No wetting or drying, sloped beds, inflow or outflow.
- Linear, small-amplitude waves only: no advection, breaking, splash or dispersion beyond the grid's. The heave case passes at 1% only because the spar is slender; a squat body in shallow water does not meet it.
- No added mass, lift or viscosity. Drag is a model with a coefficient you set: the terminal-velocity case checks the force balance, not the drag coefficient.
- Each body sees one plane of water averaged over a kernel about twice its size. Waves shorter than the body are averaged away; bodies do not shelter each other.
- Boxes, spheres and capsules only, one shape per body. Hulls and meshes are not coupled.
- CPU only; the WebGPU closed-water solver is not coupled. A scene file can describe a basin (see the simulation domain); the Lab and the Studio do not run it.

### What is not validated: cables and frames carrying rigid bodies

- Contact between bodies and members. A free body does not collide with a cable or a beam; cables have no collisions at all.
- Cable bending and torsion. Cables are axial and tension-only; an attachment transmits force, never a moment.
- Frame nonlinearity: no buckling, yielding or geometric stiffness, and a clamped body's rotation is meaningful for small rotations only.
- Other constraints on an attached body. The interface uses the body's free response, so a cable to a body that also rests on the ground reads a wrong small tension (measured 97 N to 221 N where the true value is about 0).
- The cable step is implicit Euler: first order and numerically damped (the cable pendulum loses about a fifth of its swing energy in 20 s).
- Attachments between nodes, gyroscopic terms, step-size changes and checkpoints of the coupling state.

## Cable-stayed bridge (SI scene)

The Physics Lab's bridge scene as a whole: dead-load reactions and the levelled deck, a hand-solved propped span with its mesh study, symmetry, influence lines, the first frequencies, dynamic amplification, a stay failure, wind and repeatability.

Solver: `src/engine/si-bridge.ts`: frame elements for deck and towers, compliant cables for the stays and a rigid body for the vehicle, coupled by `StructureCoupling`; 120 Hz, 4 sub-steps. 30 cases, 30 pass. Model and limits: [SI_BRIDGE.md](./SI_BRIDGE.md).

Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "symmetry: a symmetric bridge answers symmetrically, and mirrored vehicles give mirrored results".
- **Mirrored vehicles give mirrored deflections** (`si-bridge.symmetry.deflection`): largest difference between mirror-image deck nodes. Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "symmetry: a symmetric bridge answers symmetrically, and mirrored vehicles give mirrored results".
- **Slow crossing: midspan deflection follows its influence line** (`si-bridge.influence.deflection`): worst error / peak of the influence line. 20 t at 3 m/s, frame damped at 6 /s. The error is the lag of a damped structure behind the load (about 0.14 m of travel) and the ripple of the motion. Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "influence lines: a slow crossing traces the static solution at every position".
- **Slow crossing: a stay tension follows its influence line** (`si-bridge.influence.tension`): worst error / peak of the influence line. Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "influence lines: a slow crossing traces the static solution at every position".
- **First vertical mode: time-stepped against the eigenvalue solve** (`si-bridge.frequency.vertical`): frequency. Released from 200 kN at midspan, 8 s, modal coordinate. The midpoint rule runs slow by (w dt)^2 / 12 and the stays add as much. Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "dynamics: the fundamental vertical frequency against the eigenvalue solve and a hand Rayleigh estimate, and the dynamic amplification of a fast crossing".
- **First vertical mode: Rayleigh by hand with the dead-load shape** (`si-bridge.frequency.rayleigh`): Rayleigh estimate / eigenvalue frequency. A coarse shape: the weight puts the side spans down with the main span, the mode lifts them. Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "dynamics: the fundamental vertical frequency against the eigenvalue solve and a hand Rayleigh estimate, and the dynamic amplification of a fast crossing".
- **First vertical mode: Rayleigh with two Stodola refinements** (`si-bridge.frequency.stodola`): frequency. What is left is the lumping of the deck mass and the tower mass the hand method leaves out. Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "dynamics: the fundamental vertical frequency against the eigenvalue solve and a hand Rayleigh estimate, and the dynamic amplification of a fast crossing".
- **Lowest mode: lateral sway of the deck** (`si-bridge.frequency.lateral`): frequency. The stays add a little pendulum stiffness and their mass. Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "dynamics: the fundamental vertical frequency against the eigenvalue solve and a hand Rayleigh estimate, and the dynamic amplification of a fast crossing".
- **Crossing at 20 m/s: dynamic amplification is at least 1** (`si-bridge.amplification.low`): peak midspan deflection / static peak. 0.02 is allowed for the lag of the model's own damping (about 1 % of critical at 120 Hz). Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "dynamics: the fundamental vertical frequency against the eigenvalue solve and a hand Rayleigh estimate, and the dynamic amplification of a fast crossing".
- **Crossing at 20 m/s: amplification stays under the envelope** (`si-bridge.amplification.envelope20`): peak midspan deflection / static peak. Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "dynamics: the fundamental vertical frequency against the eigenvalue solve and a hand Rayleigh estimate, and the dynamic amplification of a fast crossing".
- **Crossing at 40 m/s: amplification stays under the envelope** (`si-bridge.amplification.envelope40`): peak midspan deflection / static peak. The envelope is that of a force crossing a simple span; this deck is continuous over three spans, so the load comes on smoothly. Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "dynamics: the fundamental vertical frequency against the eigenvalue solve and a hand Rayleigh estimate, and the dynamic amplification of a fast crossing".
- **A stay fails: the others reach the damaged static solution** (`si-bridge.failure.tensions`): largest stay tension error (fraction). Stay 8 of 16 (502 kN) lets go at 0.5 s; mean over the tenth second. Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "stay failure: the load moves to the neighbours as the damaged statics say, the reactions stay, the energy never grows".
- **A stay fails: its neighbour takes the load the statics say** (`si-bridge.failure.neighbour`): tension of the neighbouring stay. From 197 kN before to 333 kN after: 69 % more. Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "stay failure: the load moves to the neighbours as the damaged statics say, the reactions stay, the energy never grows".
- **A stay fails: the supports carry the same weight** (`si-bridge.failure.reaction`): sum of vertical reactions / total weight. Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "stay failure: the load moves to the neighbours as the damaged statics say, the reactions stay, the energy never grows".
- **A stay fails: the energy never grows** (`si-bridge.failure.energy`): largest rise between steps / total energy. The released strain energy is lost in the cable solver's implicit step; after that the total only falls. Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "stay failure: the load moves to the neighbours as the damaged statics say, the reactions stay, the energy never grows".
- **Wind 2 kN/m: lateral deflection, time-stepped against statics** (`si-bridge.wind.statics`): lateral deflection at midspan. Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "wind: a static lateral load bends the deck sideways and reaches the abutments".
- **Wind 2 kN/m: lateral deflection against a bare beam** (`si-bridge.wind.beam`): lateral deflection at midspan. The stays hold the deck back like pendulums of stiffness T / length, so the model is below the bare beam. Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "wind: a static lateral load bends the deck sideways and reaches the abutments".
- **Wind 2 kN/m: the supports take the whole load** (`si-bridge.wind.reaction`): sum of lateral reactions / (q L). Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "wind: a static lateral load bends the deck sideways and reaches the abutments".
- **Two runs with a vehicle, wind and a failing stay** (`si-bridge.determinism`): differing bytes of the final state. Test: [`tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/physics/si-bridge.test.mjs), "determinism: two runs with a crossing vehicle, wind and a failing stay are bit-identical".

</details>

### What is not validated: cable-stayed bridge (si scene)

- Contact between wheels and deck. The vehicle is one rigid body pinned to the two deck nodes it stands between and moved by re-attachment; it has no wheels, no suspension and no velocity along the deck.
- The vehicle's weight is shared by the lever rule: 1.9 % of the peak midspan deflection and 2.3 % of the peak stay-tension change on the default 6 m elements. Its rigid body also acts as a strut along the element it stands on (up to 8e-4 of a stay tension in the hand case).
- Buckling, yielding, geometric stiffness of the deck and towers, and cable sag (one segment per stay). The utilisation ratios are linear-elastic indicators, not a design check.
- Aerodynamics: wind is a static lateral load. No vortex shedding, flutter or buffeting.
- The reference for most rows is a second solver in the same file that shares the element matrices and the stay law. Only the propped span, the lateral frequency, the Rayleigh estimates and the wind beam are independent hand results.
- Section properties are hand estimates for a plausible steel footbridge, not a designed or surveyed bridge, and nothing is calibrated against measurements.
- The amplification rows bound the factor; they do not compare it with a moving-load solution. Damping is the model's own (about 1 % of critical in the first vertical mode at 120 Hz) plus what is set.

Solver: `box3d-webgpu-kit/geometry`: OBJ, STL and glTF/GLB readers, mesh measures, convex hulls and greedy convex decomposition. 20 cases, 20 pass. Model and limits: [README.md](../packages/box3d-kit/README.md).

### What is not validated: geometry import, hulls and decomposition

- Curved concavities are only approached by the decomposition: a torus is off by 24% with 8 hulls, 9% with 16 and 3% with 32. Only solids with flat inner faces split exactly, and only those have rows here.
- A hull body keeps at most 64 points (44 for a hull of triangles): a decimated sphere hull is smaller than the sphere. Mass is corrected to the mesh volume; the collision shape is not.
- Every fixture is generated by the tests. Files written by CAD or DCC tools, glTF extensions, materials and animations are not part of this check.
- Inertia tensors of imported shapes are not compared with a reference; only mass and volume are.
- No URDF or MJCF import yet.

### What is not validated: scene files and share links

- A save is not a bit-exact continuation. It restores poses and velocities, not the solver's warm-start impulses, sleep state or tick count; the drift rows show how far a resumed run moves in 100 ticks (up to 7 cm for a toppling ragdoll).
- Settings changed on the world after loading (motors, damping) are not saved.
- The domino, car and ragdoll example scenes are tested for behaviour, not against a closed-form number.
- The Lab and the Studio do not read scene links yet.

## One stepping loop: coupled scenes and links

Bit-identity with the modules driven by hand, a moored buoy and a cable-stayed deck loaded from scene files against closed-form statics, the heat-to-solid and weight-to-solid links, the energy ledger, and what a save of a coupled scene restores.

Solver: `box3d-webgpu-kit/simulation`: one Simulation that steps the rigid world, the water and structure couplings, heat and solids in fixed stages, and builds scenes with water, cable and frame sections. 26 cases, 26 pass. Model and limits: [SIMULATION.md](./SIMULATION.md).

<details><summary>What each case measures, and the test that asserts it</summary>

- **Moored buoy: Simulation of the scene file against the modules driven by hand** (`simulation.identity.water-structure`): checkpoints (every 60 of 480 steps) at which the world hash or the water and cable bits differ. Bit-identity is exact or it is not; the test file proves it for each adapter alone and for five solvers together. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs), "bit-identity, combined: water + structure + heat + solid with the thermal link, registered in any order, equal the hand-driven sequence".
- **Moored buoy at rest: force of the cable on the buoy** (`simulation.buoy.cable-force`): vertical force of the mooring on an 80.4 kg sphere, half-second mean. V_sub is the submerged volume the water coupling reports; the rigid solver holds mass and gravity in float32. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs), "moored buoy at rest: cable tension = rho g V_sub - weight, the draught follows, and the floor and the anchor carry the total weight".
- **Moored buoy at rest: cable tension** (`simulation.buoy.tension`): tension of the one-segment mooring (EA = 5e4 N), half-second mean. The structure coupling's free response of a body has gravity only, not the buoyancy B: the cable sees the buoy B dt^2 / m = 0.46 mm lower than it goes, and its end node m_n is carried as if the buoy fell, which adds m_n B / (m + m_n) = 0.73 N to the tension. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs), "moored buoy at rest: cable tension = rho g V_sub - weight, the draught follows, and the floor and the anchor carry the total weight".
- **Moored buoy at rest: draught** (`simulation.buoy.draught`): draught of the sphere (R = 0.4 m) against the closed-form equilibrium of cable stretch, level rise and cap volume. The structure coupling's free response of a body has gravity only, not the buoyancy B: the cable sees the buoy B dt^2 / m = 0.46 mm lower than it goes, and its end node m_n is carried as if the buoy fell, which adds m_n B / (m + m_n) = 0.73 N to the tension. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs), "moored buoy at rest: cable tension = rho g V_sub - weight, the draught follows, and the floor and the anchor carry the total weight".
- **Moored buoy at rest: tension against the closed-form equilibrium** (`simulation.buoy.tension-closed-form`): cable tension against the root of the equilibrium equation. The draught offset above times the waterplane stiffness rho g A_wp = 4.0 kN/m, plus the 0.73 N. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs), "moored buoy at rest: cable tension = rho g V_sub - weight, the draught follows, and the floor and the anchor carry the total weight".
- **Moored buoy at rest: the floor and the anchor carry the total weight** (`simulation.buoy.vertical-balance`): hydrostatic floor load minus the anchor pull. The same 0.73 N, on 1.88 MN. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs), "moored buoy at rest: cable tension = rho g V_sub - weight, the draught follows, and the floor and the anchor carry the total weight".
- **Moored buoy released 0.4 m to the side: where it ends** (`simulation.buoy.return`): distance from the anchor line after 24 s (linear drag 200 N s/m, bottom friction 0.5 /s). What the sloshing it started still moves it by; 0.5% of the offset. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs), "moored buoy released 0.4 m to the side: bounded, decaying with the drag, back at the equilibrium; the ledger with drag only falls".
- **Moored buoy released 0.4 m to the side: rest height** (`simulation.buoy.rest-height`): height of the buoy after 24 s against the run started on the anchor line. - **Moored buoy released 0.4 m to the side: bounded** (`simulation.buoy.bounded`): largest distance from the anchor line during 24 s. - **Heat to solid: a free block grows by alpha dT** (`simulation.thermal.free-expansion`): strain of a steel block 12.5 x 10 x 7.5 mm heated 80 K by the heat solver, from its far corner. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs), "rigid -> solid dead load (one-way): a block under a resting body shortens by m g L / (E A) with stress -m g / A; the body is not moved".
- **Energy ledger: a midpoint, linear solid** (`simulation.energy.solid`): largest relative change of the solid entry over 480 steps. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs), "energy ledger, undamped: conserved to the stated order of the integrators and never growing".
- **Energy ledger: heat with a fixed face, a film and a source** (`simulation.energy.heat`): largest change of stored energy minus the heat exchanged, as a fraction of the heat exchanged. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs), "energy ledger, undamped: conserved to the stated order of the integrators and never growing".
- **Energy ledger: a pendulum on a cable never gains** (`simulation.energy.pendulum-rise`): largest rise of the ledger between quarter-second samples over 6 s, as a fraction of the swing energy. The bound is float32 noise of the body state. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs), "energy ledger, undamped: conserved to the stated order of the integrators and never growing".
- **Energy ledger: the cable step is first order** (`simulation.energy.pendulum-order`): energy lost in 6 s at 240 Hz divided by the loss at 480 Hz. Implicit Euler damps the swing at (n + 1) / (4 n) omega^2 dt per second for n rigid sub-steps. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs), "energy ledger, undamped: conserved to the stated order of the integrators and never growing".
- **Save and resume, moored buoy: body** (`simulation.resume.buoy`): distance between the buoy of a run saved at tick 240 and resumed, and the original, 240 ticks later. A save does not carry the coupling's impulses, the cable multipliers or the last step's displaced volume. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs), "determinism: a coupled scene repeats bit for bit; save -> load -> continue starts from the same fields and stays within a stated bound".
- **Save and resume, moored buoy: water** (`simulation.resume.buoy-water`): largest difference of the surface elevation, same runs (waves 2.3 mm high). Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs), "determinism: a coupled scene repeats bit for bit; save -> load -> continue starts from the same fields and stays within a stated bound".
- **Save and resume, cable-stayed deck: deck** (`simulation.resume.deck`): largest difference of a deck displacement between a resumed run and the original, 240 ticks after the save. The saved velocity of a body on a frame lacks the closing half of the last frame impulse (g dt / 2 = 0.02 m/s). Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v14-simulation.test.mjs), "determinism: a coupled scene repeats bit for bit; save -> load -> continue starts from the same fields and stays within a stated bound".

</details>

### What is not validated: one stepping loop: coupled scenes and links

- Water and structure do not know of each other: the structure coupling's free response of a body has gravity only. A moored buoy's cable tension is high by m_n B / (m + m_n) (0.73 N of 1337 N here) and its draught off by B dt^2 / m (0.46 mm); a heavy cable node on a light buoy makes both larger.
- The two links are one-way. Heat drives the solid's thermal strain and a rigid body's weight loads a solid; the solid does not change the temperature, hold the body up or push it. There is no contact between rigid bodies and deformable solids.
- The thermal link needs co-located grids: a box mesh whose cells are the heat grid's cells. Only uniform end states are checked, where the mapping is exact.
- A save of a coupled scene is not a bit-exact continuation: the structure coupling's impulses and pending half kick, the cable multipliers and one step of displaced volume are not saved. The resume rows show the drift.
- The energy ledger is a sum of what each solver reports. With drag it may exceed its start by the sampling offset rho g V v dt, because its terms are known half a step apart.
- The Physics Lab and the Studio do not run coupled scenes; the Lab refuses a scene with water, cable or frame sections. Heat and solids are not in the scene format.

## Robot import (URDF and MJCF)

Forward kinematics against the product of joint transforms, the same robot from both formats, mass, the file's inertia in the solver and the gap without it, pendulum and cart-pole periods, joint limits, effort limits, joint springs and damping, a held arm, joint drift on a chain, a wheeled cart, and round trips through scene files and share links.

Solver: `box3d-webgpu-kit/robot`: URDF and MJCF files as scenes of the rigid world (one body per link, a compound when the link has several collision shapes, with the file's mass, centre of mass and inertia tensor; joints as constraints; 240 Hz, 4 sub-steps). 34 cases, 34 pass. Model and limits: [ROBOT_IMPORT.md](./ROBOT_IMPORT.md).

From the shapes alone the worst link was 42% off. - **Centre of mass: the six-joint arm has the file's** (`robot.inertia.centre-of-mass`): largest distance between a link's centre of mass in the solver and the file's inertial origin. From the shapes alone the tool link was 4.4 mm off. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs), "robot import: a link with several shapes is one compound body, and the file's inertial is what the solver holds".
- **One body per link** (`robot.compound.bodies`): bodies of the six-joint arm, whose tool link has two collision boxes. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs), "robot import: a link with several shapes is one compound body, and the file's inertial is what the solver holds".
- **A compound link from its shapes** (`robot.compound.inertia`): largest relative error of a principal moment of the two-box tool link in the solver against the sum over its boxes by parallel axes (inertia: shapes). Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs), "robot import: a link with several shapes is one compound body, and the file's inertial is what the solver holds".
- **One revolute link: the period of the file's inertia** (`robot.pendulum.file-period`): period of a 0.8 m rod hinged at its end whose file states 1.3 x the rod's transverse inertia, mean over 20 s. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs), "robot import: a hinged rod whose file states 1.3 x its shape's inertia swings with the file's period".
- **One revolute link: file inertia against shape inertia** (`robot.pendulum.file-against-shapes`): measured period with the file's inertia over the measured period with inertia: shapes, minus 1. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v17-compound.test.mjs), "robot import: a hinged rod whose file states 1.3 x its shape's inertia swings with the file's period".

</details>

### What is not validated: robot import (urdf and mjcf)

- The file's inertial is applied as numbers; the collision shapes are not changed to agree with it. A tensor that is not positive definite is not applied (the shapes' inertia is used, with a warning), and with `links: 'welded'` a link of several bodies keeps its shapes' inertia. The rows marked "inertia: shapes" measure the import without the file's inertia (42% off on the worst link of the example arm).
- Joints are soft constraints (60 Hz by default; `jointStiffness` raises it). A loaded arm settles below its kinematic pose (17 mm at the tool of the 1 m example arm) and a chain stretches by millimetres. There is no reduced-coordinate articulation solver.
- No comparison with MuJoCo, Gazebo or another simulator on the same model: every reference here is closed form.
- Mesh collision is the convex hull of each mesh; only the parser path and a cube and a tetrahedron are checked. No real robot model with meshes is in the suite.
- Ball joints, floating bases under contact, self-collision of real robots, and contact between a robot and objects (grasping) have no reference here.
- Joint springs damp numerically (measured 0.10 /s on the spring case), and joint damping without stiffness adds a very weak spring towards the starting pose.
- MJCF: equality constraints, tendons, most actuator types and several joints on one body are reported and dropped, so models that depend on them do not behave as in MuJoCo.

## Cloth: membrane, bending, contact and rigid coupling

The patch test, uniaxial stress and Poisson contraction (and the edge-spring model failing it), a hanging strip, the catenary, a cantilever with its mesh study, the frequency of a tensioned strip, a pressurised membrane, the integrators' energy, Coulomb friction on a ramp, a plate that must not tunnel, a ball on a trampoline, a draped box on a scale, a hanging body, self-collision and repeatability.

Solver: `box3d-webgpu-kit/cloth`: constant-strain St. Venant-Kirchhoff triangles, Koiter bending on the triangle-averaged shape operator, backward Euler by Newton and preconditioned conjugate gradients, float64; rigid bodies as unknowns of the same solve. 32 cases, 32 pass. Model and limits: [CLOTH.md](./CLOTH.md).

<details><summary>What each case measures, and the test that asserts it</summary>

- **Membrane patch test on an irregular mesh** (`cloth.patch.position`): largest distance of an interior node from the uniform deformation given to the boundary (49 nodes jittered by 30% of a cell). Constant-strain triangles hold a uniform deformation exactly; what is left is rounding. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "membrane patch test: a uniform strain is reproduced on an irregular mesh".
- **Uniaxial tension: stress over strain** (`cloth.uniaxial.modulus`): traction / axial strain of a free strip pulled at 10 N/m (E = 1e7 Pa, t = 1 mm, nu = 0.3). The law is St. Venant-Kirchhoff, linear in the Green strain: at a strain of 1e-3 it reads 1.5e-3 high against Hooke. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "uniaxial strip: stress = E strain and lateral contraction = -nu strain; edge springs fail it".
- **Uniaxial tension: lateral contraction** (`cloth.uniaxial.poisson`): minus lateral strain over axial strain of the same strip. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "uniaxial strip: stress = E strain and lateral contraction = -nu strain; edge springs fail it".
- **Uniaxial tension: stretch against the exact law** (`cloth.uniaxial.exact`): axial strain against the stretch l of l Y (l^2 - 1) / 2 = T. The state is uniform, so only the solve tolerance is left. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "uniaxial strip: stress = E strain and lateral contraction = -nu strain; edge springs fail it".
- **Strip hanging under its own weight** (`cloth.hanging.elongation`): elongation of a 1 m strip (0.5 kg/m^2, E t = 1e4 N/m, nu = 0), 16 elements. Lumped weights are exact at the nodes of a bar; the shortfall is the law (the top strain, 4.9e-4). Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "hanging strip: elongation rho g L^2 / (2 E t) and reaction = weight".
- **Strip hanging under its own weight: support reaction** (`cloth.hanging.reaction`): sum of the reactions on the pinned edge. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "hanging strip: elongation rho g L^2 / (2 E t) and reaction = weight".
- **Stiff strip pinned at both ends: sag** (`cloth.catenary.sag`): midspan sag of a 1.2 m strip over a 1 m span (E t = 1e6 N/m), 32 elements. A chain of straight links with lumped weights against the smooth curve. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "catenary: a stiff strip pinned at both ends sags like the inextensible catenary, converging with the mesh".
- **Stiff strip pinned at both ends: observed order** (`cloth.catenary.order`): convergence order of the sag error from 16 to 32 elements. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "catenary: a stiff strip pinned at both ends sags like the inextensible catenary, converging with the mesh".
- **Cantilevered strip under gravity: tip deflection** (`cloth.cantilever.tip`): tip deflection of a 0.2 m strip (D = 0.1667 N m, nu = 0), 32 elements along it, regular mesh. Small deflection (1.5% of the length). The clamp is a row of held triangles, counted as a mirror image. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "cantilever strip: tip deflection w L^4 / (8 D), second order on regular meshes, with the error on irregular ones stated".
- **Cantilevered strip: observed order on regular meshes** (`cloth.cantilever.order`): convergence order of the tip error from 16 to 32 elements. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "cantilever strip: tip deflection w L^4 / (8 D), second order on regular meshes, with the error on irregular ones stated".
- **Cantilevered strip on an irregular mesh** (`cloth.cantilever.irregular`): tip deflection with interior nodes jittered by 25% of a cell, 16 elements. A bound on what was measured, not accuracy: the triangle-averaged curvature is not consistent on irregular meshes and this error does not shrink with refinement (11% at 32 elements). Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "cantilever strip: tip deflection w L^4 / (8 D), second order on regular meshes, with the error on irregular ones stated".
- **Pre-tensioned strip: first transverse frequency** (`cloth.strip.frequency`): frequency of a strip stretched by 1% between pinned ends, 32 elements, midpoint rule at dt = 1/2000 s. Lumped masses lower it by (pi / n)^2 / 24; the time step by (omega dt)^2 / 12 = 7e-5. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "pre-tensioned strip: first frequency (1 / 2L) sqrt(T / rho), converging with the mesh".
- **Pre-tensioned strip: observed order** (`cloth.strip.order`): convergence order of the frequency error from 8 to 16 elements. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "pre-tensioned strip: first frequency (1 / 2L) sqrt(T / rho), converging with the mesh".
- **Pre-tensioned square membrane under pressure** (`cloth.membrane.deflection`): centre deflection, 32 cells per side (deflection 1e-3 of the side). The membrane also stiffens with deflection, by 1e-4 of the tension here. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "pressurised square membrane: centre deflection 0.0737 p a^2 / T".
- **Pre-tensioned square membrane: observed order** (`cloth.membrane.order`): convergence order of the deflection error from 8 to 16 cells per side. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "pressurised square membrane: centre deflection 0.0737 p a^2 / T".
- **Backward Euler: energy left in a mode** (`cloth.energy.backward-euler`): energy of the strip mode after 0.5 s over its start, dt = 1/1000 s. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "energy: backward Euler loses 1 / (1 + (omega dt)^2) per step, the midpoint rule conserves".
- **Midpoint rule: energy drift** (`cloth.energy.midpoint`): largest change of the mode energy over 250 steps at dt = 1/500 s, over that energy. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "energy: backward Euler loses 1 / (1 + (omega dt)^2) per step, the midpoint rule conserves".
- **Cloth patch sliding on a 30 degree ramp** (`cloth.friction.slide`): speed down the ramp after 0.5 s, mu = 0.3. - **Cloth patch on a ramp below the friction angle** (`cloth.friction.stick`): speed after 1 s at 26 degrees with mu = 0.5 (tan = 0.488). Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "friction on an incline: sticks below tan(theta) = mu, slides at g (sin - mu cos) above".
- **Cloth patch just above the friction angle** (`cloth.friction.threshold`): speed after 1 s at 27 degrees with mu = 0.5 (tan = 0.510). The acceleration is the difference of two forces fifty times larger. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "friction on an incline: sticks below tan(theta) = mu, slides at g (sin - mu cos) above".
- **Thin kinematic plate through a cloth at 200 m/s** (`cloth.tunnelling.plate`): nodes left behind a 2 mm plate that travels 0.83 m in one step of 1/240 s. Nodes against flat faces only. A curved body is safe while it moves less than about its radius per step; body corners between nodes are not seen. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "no tunnelling: a thin kinematic plate sweeps a cloth at up to 200 m/s".
- **Ball bouncing on a pinned cloth: momentum** (`cloth.trampoline.momentum`): momentum change of ball + cloth less the impulse of gravity and the supports over 1.25 s, over the momentum exchanged. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "trampoline: momentum balances, reactions carry the weight at rest, rest depth matches statics".
- **Ball at rest on a pinned cloth: support reactions** (`cloth.trampoline.reaction`): sum of the edge reactions with a 2.69 kg ball resting on a 0.3 kg cloth, quarter-second mean. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "trampoline: momentum balances, reactions carry the weight at rest, rest depth matches statics".
- **Ball at rest on a pinned cloth: height against statics** (`cloth.trampoline.depth`): height of the ball centre (the cloth sags 97 mm under it), time-stepped to rest. The reference is the same model solved another way: it checks the coupled time stepping, not the model. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "trampoline: momentum balances, reactions carry the weight at rest, rest depth matches statics".
- **Cloth draped over a box on a spring scale** (`cloth.scale.reading`): extra load read from the extra sag of the spring joint under the box (0.81 kg cloth overhanging a 14.4 kg box). The 1.55 mm sag is a float32 position of the rigid world. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "a cloth draped over a box on a spring scale adds exactly its weight".
- **Box hanging from a strip** (`cloth.attachment.stretch`): stretch of a 1 m strip (E t = 1e5 N/m, 0.2 m wide) carrying a 4 kg box attached along its lower edge. The 0.3% is the law at a strain of 2e-3; against the exact law the test allows 2.5e-7 m (float32 of the body position). Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "a body hanging from a strip stretches it by m g L / (E t w)".
- **Light body on a stiff strip: bounded** (`cloth.attachment.light-body`): fastest speed in 1 s of a 40 g box released on a strip with k dt^2 / m = 868, over the physical bound g dt / sqrt(k dt^2 / m). The naive staggered scheme overflows float32 in the same set-up (from a ratio of about 3). Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "a light body on a stiff cloth is stable; naive staggering blows up".
- **Three sheets stacked on a plane: support force** (`cloth.self.stack`): force on the plane under three separate 0.3 m sheets resting on each other by self-collision. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "self-collision: stacked sheets carry their weight a thickness apart".
- **Three sheets stacked on a plane: spacing** (`cloth.self.stack-gap`): smallest node-to-triangle distance between sheets, in collision thicknesses (4 mm). Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "self-collision: stacked sheets carry their weight a thickness apart".
- **Folded strip pressed by a box: layers stay apart** (`cloth.self.fold`): smallest distance between the two layers during the drop of a 0.34 kg box, in collision thicknesses. Sampled every sixth step. Without self-collision the same box presses the layers through each other. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "self-collision: a folded cloth pressed by a box keeps its layers apart".
- **Folded strip pressed by a box: support force** (`cloth.self.fold-support`): force on the plane under the fold and the box. Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "self-collision: a folded cloth pressed by a box keeps its layers apart".

Test: [`packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/packages/box3d-kit/test/v16-cloth.test.mjs), "determinism: repeat runs are bit-identical, and the Simulation loop adds nothing".

</details>

### What is not validated: cloth: membrane, bending, contact and rigid coupling

- Bending on irregular meshes. The triangle-averaged curvature is consistent on structured meshes only: with nodes jittered by 25% of a cell the cantilever is 4% too stiff at 16 elements and 11% at 32, and refinement does not help. The membrane rows do not have this limit.
- Large strains and wrinkling. The membrane law is St. Venant-Kirchhoff, checked at strains up to 2e-3; it is not a fabric model (no anisotropy, no warp and weft, no hysteresis), and compression is carried until the sheet buckles at the scale of the mesh.
- Tearing, plasticity and damage are not modelled. Bending stiffness of a woven fabric is not E t^3 / 12: it must be measured and set.
- Contact is node against body: a body corner or edge between nodes is not seen, a body smaller than the mesh spacing rests on single nodes, and hulls, triangle meshes and height fields are not supported. Curved bodies are safe from tunnelling only below about one radius of travel per step.
- Self-collision is a repulsion without friction, checked for layers pressed at 0.02 N per pair. It is not intersection-free: a pair pressed harder than stiffness times thickness, or one that closes by more than a mesh edge in one step, can pass through, and nothing untangles it.
- Friction limits lag the normal force by a Newton iterate in transients; only steady sliding and sticking are checked. Rolling and spinning friction are not modelled.
- The coupling sees a body's other contacts and joints only through an estimate that lags one step. A cloth heavier than the supported body it rests on is not checked. Bodies rotate by a linearised rotation in the contact geometry (error (omega dt)^2 / 2 times the body size per step).
- Wind is a normal-pressure formula, not aerodynamics, and has no reference here beyond its own force. No real-fabric measurement is used anywhere: every reference is a formula.

### What is not validated: heat conduction

- Conduction in solids only: no phase change, no fluid flow, no convection beyond a film coefficient you supply, no radiation between surfaces (no view factors), no contact resistance.
- Curved or slanted surfaces are stair-stepped by the grid, which makes their area wrong (a 45 degree face is too large by sqrt(2)). Every case here has axis-aligned faces.
- Crank-Nicolson overshoots after a sudden change when alpha dt / h^2 is large (452 K next to a 400 K surface at 8.2); the erfc rows use a step where it does not.
- k(T) is lagged by one step and radiation is linearised once per step: first order in dt for strongly nonlinear cases.
- The thermal-stress rows are one-way formulas for full restraint, not a stress analysis.
- Material data are inputs: no calibrated material library is validated here. Not in the scene format, and not used by the Lab or the Studio.

### What is not validated: deformable solids

- Bending is where this element is weak, and the table shows it: one cell through the thickness is three times too stiff, four cells 12%, eight cells 3.4%. Bending frequencies are 5% to 6% high at four cells.
- Near-incompressibility: at nu = 0.4999 the four-cell cantilever is 29% too stiff. There is no mixed or higher-order element.
- With nu = 0.3 a clamped root also restrains Poisson contraction, which beam theory ignores: the 3-D limit sits about 1.2% below the Timoshenko reference.
- Contact and self-contact, plasticity, viscoelasticity, anisotropy, and more than one material per body. Crack growth is a separate solver on the linear model of this element (the fracture domain); `SolidBody` itself only flags elements above a strength.
- No two-way coupling to the rigid-body, water, cable or frame solvers, and no contact with rigid bodies. The one-way thermal and dead-load links are in the simulation domain.
- Uniform states are exact, so the tension, shear, pressure and rubber rows say nothing about accuracy under stress gradients.

## Fracture of deformable solids

A bar with a weak cross-section against the traction-separation law and G_c A, mesh objectivity of the cohesive and crack-band energies, a centre-cracked plate against Griffith, a notched beam against the size-effect law and the work of fracture, momentum and energy of a bar that breaks in flight, the onset of thermal-shock cracking against the heat module, and the mesh dependence of an inclined crack.

Solver: `src/engine/solid-fracture.ts`: small-strain linear tetrahedra with cohesive interfaces on element faces (bilinear traction-separation law, nodes duplicated where a face opens) or a Rankine crack band; static, midpoint, backward-Euler and explicit integration, float64. 18 cases, 18 pass. Model and limits: [SOLID_FRACTURE.md](./SOLID_FRACTURE.md).

| Case | Reference | Measured | Error | Tolerance | Result |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Cohesive bar: peak load | `sigma_c` = 3000000 Pa | 3000000 | -1.24e-12 rel. | ±1e-9 rel. | pass |
| Cohesive bar: softening law | `linear softening to delta_c = 2 G_c / sigma_c` = 0 | 1.079248e-12 | +1.08e-12 | ±1e-8 | pass |
| Cohesive bar: fracture energy | `G_c A` = 0.25 J | 0.25 | -5.55e-16 rel. | ±1e-9 rel. | pass |
| Cohesive bar: work to break it | `G_c A` = 0.25 J | 0.2500113 | +4.51e-5 rel. | ±0.1% | pass |
| Cohesive bar: energy released when an interface is inserted under load | `T_before T_after / (2 K G_c) = (delta_0 / delta_c) (1 + E delta_0 / (sigma_c L))` = 0.02133333 | 0.02133333 | +9.43e-15 rel. | ±1e-6 rel. | pass |
| Crack band: fracture energy with regularisation | `G_c A` = 0.25 J | 0.2500114 | +4.58e-5 rel. | ±1% | pass |

| Griffith: centre-cracked plate, cells of l_ch | `sqrt(E G_c) / (Y sqrt(pi a)), Y = sqrt(sec(pi a / (2 b)))` = 727560.3 Pa | 811229.7 | +11.5% | ±15% | pass |
| Griffith: centre-cracked plate, cells of l_ch / 2 | `sqrt(E G_c) / (Y sqrt(pi a))` = 727560.3 Pa | 702095.7 | -3.5% | ±5% | pass |

<details><summary>What each case measures, and the test that asserts it</summary>

- **Cohesive bar: peak load** (`fracture.bar.peak`): peak stress of a 0.2 m bar with a weak cross-section, cohesive interface, 8 x 2 x 2 cells. A load step lands on the peak, U = sigma_c L / E + delta_0; the stress is uniform, so only the solver tolerance remains. Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "uniaxial bar with a weak interface: peak sigma_c A, linear softening, G_c A dissipated, damaged secant, zero traction when broken".
- **Cohesive bar: softening law** (`fracture.bar.softening`): largest difference between the bar stress and sigma_c (delta_c - delta) / (delta_c - delta_0) at the measured opening, over 40 load steps, divided by sigma_c. Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "uniaxial bar with a weak interface: peak sigma_c A, linear softening, G_c A dissipated, damaged secant, zero traction when broken".
- **Cohesive bar: fracture energy** (`fracture.bar.energy`): energy dissipated when the bar has separated. Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "uniaxial bar with a weak interface: peak sigma_c A, linear softening, G_c A dissipated, damaged secant, zero traction when broken".
- **Cohesive bar: work to break it** (`fracture.bar.work`): area under the load-displacement curve of the same bar. Trapezoid rule over the load steps; the error is in the two steps that hold a kink of the curve. Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "uniaxial bar with a weak interface: peak sigma_c A, linear softening, G_c A dissipated, damaged secant, zero traction when broken".
- **Cohesive bar: energy released when an interface is inserted under load** (`fracture.bar.insertion-loss`): relaxation the ledger books when the solver inserts the interface of the same bar itself, divided by G_c A. An interface inserted at a loaded face adds its compliance at once. The work to break this bar is 2.1 % above G_c A for that reason; the dissipated energy is still G_c A. Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "mesh objectivity: a through-crack dissipates G_c A on three meshes; the crack band needs its regularisation for that".
- **Crack band: fracture energy with regularisation** (`fracture.band.regularised`): work to break a bar with a weak layer of 12.5 mm cells, nu = 0. Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "mesh objectivity: a through-crack dissipates G_c A on three meshes; the crack band needs its regularisation for that".
- **Crack band: mesh objectivity** (`fracture.band.objectivity`): work to break the bar on 50 mm cells divided by that on 12.5 mm cells, with regularisation. Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "mesh objectivity: a through-crack dissipates G_c A on three meshes; the crack band needs its regularisation for that".
- **Crack band without regularisation: mesh dependence** (`fracture.band.unregularised`): the same ratio with a fixed failure strain. Shown as a failure of the unregularised model: its dissipated energy is proportional to the element size. Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "mesh objectivity: a through-crack dissipates G_c A on three meshes; the crack band needs its regularisation for that".
- **Griffith: centre-cracked plate, cells of l_ch** (`fracture.griffith.coarse`): remote stress at which a crack of half-length 5 l_ch runs, cells of l_ch at the tip. Too coarse on purpose: 0.42 cells per process-zone length c_f. The plate reads 11.5 % strong. Load steps of 1 % of the reference. Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "Griffith: a centre-cracked plate fails at K_Ic / (Y sqrt(pi a)) with K_Ic = sqrt(E G_c), within the stated band".
- **Griffith: centre-cracked plate, cells of l_ch / 2** (`fracture.griffith.fine`): the same with cells of l_ch / 2. A cohesive crack of this size is weaker than LEFM because of its process zone: refined meshes converge to 0.955 of the reference (see the next row and docs/SOLID_FRACTURE.md). Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "Griffith: a centre-cracked plate fails at K_Ic / (Y sqrt(pi a)) with K_Ic = sqrt(E G_c), within the stated band".
- **Griffith with the process zone** (`fracture.griffith.effective-crack`): the same against LEFM for the crack a + c_f, c_f = 0.419 l_ch. Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "Griffith: a centre-cracked plate fails at K_Ic / (Y sqrt(pi a)) with K_Ic = sqrt(E G_c), within the stated band".
- **Notched beam: work of fracture** (`fracture.beam.work`): area under the load-deflection curve of a beam of depth 0.6 l_ch, 6 cells in the ligament. The node row under the load is the hinge and never opens, so half a cell of the ligament stays whole: 8.3 % of G_c times the ligament here, 12.5 % with 4 cells. Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "notched three-point bending: peak load against LEFM and the size-effect law, and the work of fracture against G_c times the ligament".
- **Notched beam: peak load** (`fracture.beam.peak`): peak load of a beam of depth 2.4 l_ch, 8 cells through the depth. The law is an asymptote for large beams: measured +9 % at 2.4 l_ch with 8 cells, +6 % with 12 cells and +1 % at 4.8 l_ch. The LEFM load is an upper bound (0.75 of it here). Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "notched three-point bending: peak load against LEFM and the size-effect law, and the work of fracture against G_c times the ligament".
- **Free flight: linear momentum** (`fracture.flight.linear-momentum`): largest change of the linear momentum of a bar that breaks in flight, divided by m V. Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "mass and momentum: node splitting and the fragment hand-off conserve them; a bar broken in free flight keeps its momentum".
- **Free flight: angular momentum of a spinning bar** (`fracture.flight.angular-momentum`): largest change of the angular momentum of the bar spinning at 40 rad/s, divided by m V L. Small-strain elements: forces act along reference directions, so angular momentum is kept only to the order of the rotation times the strain. Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "mass and momentum: node splitting and the fragment hand-off conserve them; a bar broken in free flight keeps its momentum".
- **Free flight: energy balance** (`fracture.flight.energy`): largest energy imbalance of the explicit run at 0.8 of the stability limit, divided by the initial kinetic energy. Second order in the time step: 1.2e-4, 2.9e-5 and 8e-6 at 0.8, 0.4 and 0.2 of the limit. Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "energy balance: external work = strain + interface + kinetic + dissipated energy, quasi-static and dynamic".
- **Thermal shock: time of the first crack** (`fracture.thermal.onset`): time at which the quenched plate first cracks. The solid reads element temperatures that average in the second cell layer, so it cracks a few steps later. Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "thermal shock: the heat solver cracks the quenched plate at its cooled face when the heat module says the surface stress reaches the strength".
- **Crack path: a crack inclined 30 degrees to the mesh** (`fracture.path.area`): crack area divided by the area of the inclined plane, five-tetrahedron cells. Shown as a limit: the crack follows faces, so it is 24 % larger than the plane on this mesh and 48 % on six-tetrahedron cells, at any resolution. Test: [`tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/solid-fracture.test.mjs), "crack paths follow element faces: the area and energy of a crack inclined to the mesh depend on the mesh".

</details>

### What is not validated: fracture of deformable solids

- Crack paths. A cohesive crack can only follow element faces: a crack inclined 30 degrees to the mesh is 24 % (five-tetrahedron cells) or 48 % (six-tetrahedron cells) larger than the plane it should follow, at any resolution, and dissipates 30 % to 70 % too much energy. Every closed-form row here has its crack on a mesh plane.
- Insertion on demand near a crack tip. The criterion reads the mean stress of two elements, which misses the peak at a tip: with cells of l_ch / 2 the centre-cracked plate fails at 1.60 of the Griffith stress unless interfaces are inserted earlier (0.5 sigma_c gives 0.985) or placed along the expected path, as the Griffith and beam rows do.
- The Griffith and beam rows are converged in neither mesh nor size: cells of l_ch read 11.5 % high, cells of l_ch / 2 read 3.5 % low, and the cohesive law itself is 4.5 % below LEFM at a = 5 l_ch (1.5 % at 10 l_ch). The size-effect law used for the beam is an asymptote, and its constant c_f = 0.419 l_ch is taken from the literature.
- Crack branching, dynamic crack speeds and fragmentation statistics have no reference here; branching is whatever the faces allow. No plasticity, no rate dependence, no fatigue.
- Contact exists only across an interface (a penalty that stops its two sides passing through each other, without friction). Fragments do not collide with each other or with anything else until they are handed to the rigid world, and that hand-off is one-way.
- Small strain: a piece that rotates after breaking off carries false stress (angular momentum of a bar spinning at 40 rad/s drifts by 1.5e-4 of m V L). The crack band uses isotropic damage: it weakens compression too, and a band held sideways by its neighbours dissipates 0.9 G_c at nu = 0.2.
- The thermal-shock row checks when and where the first crack appears, on elements larger than l_ch; the crack pattern after that (spacing, depth, arrest) is not resolved and has no row. The heat flow does not see the cracks.

Cantilever compliance in all six directions, self-weight deflection, an exact discrete oscillator, the first bending mode and the temporal order.

Solver: `src/engine/frame-runtime.ts`: Euler-Bernoulli elements with cubic Hermite bending, consistent mass, implicit midpoint, float64. 16 cases, 16 pass. Model and limits: [FRAME_MECHANICS.md](./FRAME_MECHANICS.md).

### What is not validated: frames (beam finite elements)

- Transverse shear and bending rotary inertia (Euler-Bernoulli, not Timoshenko): deep beams are too stiff.
- Geometric stiffness, finite rotations and buckling. The solver flags rotations above 0.1 rad and strains above 0.01; it does not model them.
- Yielding, fracture and contact.
- The static rows are exact for this element, so they check the implementation rather than convergence; only the bending mode tests the discretisation.
- The evidence runs under docs/FRAME_MECHANICS.md are not in the repository; these rows are measured fresh instead.

## Cables

A taut link against an independent implicit solve, the order in the time step, a hanging cable, curved motion, and a suspended span against statics and the extensible catenary.

Solver: `src/engine/compliant-cable.ts`: tension-only axial links, XPBD (`cable-xpbd-js-f64-v1`) and proximal nonlinear (`cable-proximal-js-f64-v2`) backends, implicit Euler, float64. 12 cases, 12 pass. Model and limits: [COMPLIANT_CABLE.md](./COMPLIANT_CABLE.md), [NONLINEAR_CABLE.md](./NONLINEAR_CABLE.md).

| Case | Reference | Measured | Error | Tolerance | Result |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| One taut link: extension after 2 s | `backward-Euler recurrence of m e'' = m g - k e` = 0.3242305 m | 0.3242305 | -1.89e-14 | ±2e-11 | pass |
| One taut link: tension | `T = k e` = 19.45383 N | 19.45383 | -1.14e-12 | ±2e-8 | pass |
| Axial oscillator: observed order in the step | `log2(e_480 / e_960) = 1 (implicit Euler)` = 1 | 0.9887351 | -0.0113 | ±0.13 | pass |
| Hanging cable with a tip mass: extension | `dL = g (m L + rho L^2 / 2) / (E A)` = 0.024525 m | 0.024525 | +1.87e-10 | ±2e-7 | pass |
| Hanging cable with a tip mass: support reaction | `R = (m + rho L) g` = 14.715 N | 14.715 | +1.35e-10 | ±2e-5 | pass |
| Hanging cable with a tip mass: top tension | `T = (m + rho L - rho L / (2 n)) g` = 14.10187 N | 14.10187 | +1.35e-10 | ±2e-5 | pass |
| Curved motion of a two-link cable | `bisection solve of the symmetric implicit step` = 0 m | 5.517808e-14 | +5.52e-14 | at most 1e-8 above the reference | pass |
| Suspended span: node positions | `statics: constant horizontal tension, vertical tension steps by each nodal weight` = 0 m | 4.113887e-11 | +4.11e-11 | at most 2e-7 above the reference | pass |
| Suspended span: segment tensions | `T_j = hypot(H, V_j)` = 0 N | 2.333397e-7 | +2.33e-7 | at most 2e-5 above the reference | pass |
| Suspended span: horizontal reaction | `H from the force polygon` = 19.59348 N | 19.59348 | +1.19e-7 | ±2e-5 | pass |
| Suspended span: sag against the extensible catenary | `extensible catenary with a central point load (closed-form integrals)` = 0.7597774 m | 0.7598223 | +4.5e-5 | ±4.8e-5 | pass |
| Suspended span: observed order of the sag error | `log2(e_16 / e_32) = 2` = 2 | 2.000321 | +0.000321 | ±0.1 | pass |

- **One taut link: extension after 2 s** (`cable.spring.extension`): extension of a 60 N/m link carrying 2 kg, released 0.4 m stretched (XPBD backend, dt = 1/120 s). The reference is the same implicit step solved independently as a scalar recurrence, so this checks the solve, not the time accuracy. - **Hanging cable with a tip mass: extension** (`cable.hanging.extension`): tip extension of a 2 m cable (0.25 kg/m, EA = 1000 N, 4 segments) carrying 1 kg. The lumped cable reproduces the continuum stretch on any mesh. Test: [`tests/engine/compliant-cable.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/compliant-cable.test.mjs), "distributed hanging mass preserves mesh-independent extension, total mass and support reaction".
- **Hanging cable with a tip mass: support reaction** (`cable.hanging.reaction`): vertical reaction at the anchor. Test: [`tests/engine/compliant-cable.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/compliant-cable.test.mjs), "distributed hanging mass preserves mesh-independent extension, total mass and support reaction".
- **Hanging cable with a tip mass: top tension** (`cable.hanging.tension`): tension in the top segment (the anchor node carries half a segment itself).
