- **Curved motion of a two-link cable** (`cable.curved.trajectory`): largest position error over 1 s against an independent nonlinear scalar solve (proximal backend, dt = 1/120 s). Test: [`tests/engine/proximal-cable.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/proximal-cable.test.mjs), "curved motion agrees with an independent nonlinear scalar solve, including hard constraints".
- **Suspended span: node positions** (`cable.span.shape`): largest node position error of a 32-segment span with a central mass against force-polygon shooting. Test: [`tests/engine/proximal-cable.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/proximal-cable.test.mjs), "curved spans match force-polygon shooting and converge toward the extensible catenary".
- **Suspended span: segment tensions** (`cable.span.tensions`): largest segment tension error of the same span against force-polygon shooting. Test: [`tests/engine/proximal-cable.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/proximal-cable.test.mjs), "curved spans match force-polygon shooting and converge toward the extensible catenary".
- **Suspended span: horizontal reaction** (`cable.span.horizontal`): horizontal pull at the left anchor. Test: [`tests/engine/proximal-cable.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/proximal-cable.test.mjs), "curved spans match force-polygon shooting and converge toward the extensible catenary".
- **Suspended span: sag against the extensible catenary** (`cable.span.sag`): midspan sag of the 32-segment span (4.2 m cable over a 4 m gap, EA = 1000 N, 1 kg at the middle). The test asserts the order of this error, not its size. The tolerance is the largest finest-mesh sag error docs/NONLINEAR_CABLE.md states (0.04738 mm), rounded up to 0.048 mm. Test: [`tests/engine/proximal-cable.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/proximal-cable.test.mjs), "curved spans match force-polygon shooting and converge toward the extensible catenary".
- **Suspended span: observed order of the sag error** (`cable.span.order`): convergence order of the sag error from 16 to 32 segments. The test accepts an error ratio of 3.7 to 4.3 per doubling. Test: [`tests/engine/proximal-cable.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/proximal-cable.test.mjs), "curved spans match force-polygon shooting and converge toward the extensible catenary".

</details>

### What is not validated: cables

- Bending and torsion: cables are axial and tension-only, with no material calibration.
- Time accuracy is first order and the step is numerically damped. The taut-link rows compare with the same implicit step solved independently, so they check the solve, not how close the motion is to the continuum.
- The XPBD backend approximates changing constraint directions; curved spans are validated on the proximal backend only.
- Exact angular-momentum conservation is not claimed.
- Collisions: cables do not collide with anything.
- The production Studio bridge still uses its own comparative cable model, which these rows do not cover.

## Closed-basin water

Rest, standing waves against the exact discrete and continuum solutions with the observed order, and volume and energy over 24,000 steps.

Solver: `src/engine/closed-water.ts`: linear shallow water on a staggered C-grid with closed walls, float32 fields. 8 cases, 8 pass. Model and limits: [CLOSED_WATER.md](./CLOSED_WATER.md).

| Case | Reference | Measured | Error | Tolerance | Result |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| A basin at rest stays at rest | `eta = const, u = v = 0` = 0 m, m/s | 0 | 0 | ±0 | pass |
| Standing wave against the exact discrete solution (no drag) | `eta_n = A rho^n (cos(n theta) + b sin(n theta)) cos(k_x x) cos(k_z z)` = 0 m | 1.355119e-7 | +1.36e-7 | at most 5e-6 above the reference | pass |
| Standing wave against the exact discrete solution (drag 0.28 /s) | `eta_n = A rho^n (cos(n theta) + b sin(n theta)) cos(k_x x) cos(k_z z)` = 0 m | 5.09798e-8 | +5.1e-8 | at most 5e-6 above the reference | pass |
| Standing wave against the continuum solution, 128 x 96 grid | `eta = A cos(omega t) cos(k_x x) cos(k_z z), omega^2 = g H (k_x^2 + k_z^2)` = 0 | 0.0005720307 | +0.000572 | at most 0.003 above the reference | pass |
| Standing wave: observed order | `log2(e_64 / e_128) = 2` = 2 | 1.998191 | -0.00181 | ±0.17 | pass |
| Volume conservation over 24,000 steps | `\|V(t) - V(0)\| / V_L1 = 0` = 0 | 1.890463e-7 | +1.89e-7 | at most 0.0001 above the reference | pass |
| Modified energy over 24,000 steps | `\|E~(t) / E~(0) - 1\| = 0` = 0 | 9.100525e-7 | +9.1e-7 | at most 0.0005 above the reference | pass |
| No flow through the walls | `u . n = 0 on the walls` = 0 m/s | 0 | 0 | ±0 | pass |

<details><summary>What each case measures, and the test that asserts it</summary>

- **A basin at rest stays at rest** (`closed-water.rest`): largest change of the level or of any face velocity after 1200 steps from a uniform 2 m offset (with drag). Test: [`tests/engine/closed-water.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/closed-water.test.mjs), "closed basin preserves uniform rest, including walls, without a height clamp".
- **Standing wave against the exact discrete solution (no drag)** (`closed-water.discrete-wave.undamped`): largest field error over 2400 steps (20 s) for mode (2, 1) on a 32 x 24 grid, amplitude 0.03 m. The fields are float32: the error is accumulated rounding at 0.03 m amplitude. Test: [`tests/engine/closed-water.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/closed-water.test.mjs), "closed C-grid follows independent discrete standing waves, including centered drag".
- **Standing wave against the exact discrete solution (drag 0.28 /s)** (`closed-water.discrete-wave.damped`): largest field error over 2400 steps (20 s) for mode (2, 1) on a 32 x 24 grid, amplitude 0.03 m. The fields are float32: the error is accumulated rounding at 0.03 m amplitude. Test: [`tests/engine/closed-water.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/closed-water.test.mjs), "closed C-grid follows independent discrete standing waves, including centered drag".
- **Standing wave against the continuum solution, 128 x 96 grid** (`closed-water.continuum.error`): normalised RMS error of eta, u and v after 10 s for mode (2, 1). Test: [`tests/engine/closed-water.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/closed-water.test.mjs), "continuum wave error converges at second order when space and timestep refine together".
- **Standing wave: observed order** (`closed-water.continuum.order`): convergence order of that error from 64 x 48 to 128 x 96 cells, with the time step halved too. The test accepts an error ratio of 3.5 to 4.5 per doubling. Test: [`tests/engine/closed-water.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/closed-water.test.mjs), "continuum wave error converges at second order when space and timestep refine together".
- **Volume conservation over 24,000 steps** (`closed-water.volume`): largest change of the water volume, relative to the L1 volume of the initial surface. The update conserves volume exactly in exact arithmetic; float32 storage leaves this. Test: [`tests/engine/closed-water.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/closed-water.test.mjs), "unforced closed basin conserves mass and bounded modified energy over 24000 ticks".
- **Modified energy over 24,000 steps** (`closed-water.energy`): largest relative change of the scheme's modified energy for a rough random surface. Test: [`tests/engine/closed-water.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/closed-water.test.mjs), "unforced closed basin conserves mass and bounded modified energy over 24000 ticks".
- **No flow through the walls** (`closed-water.walls`): largest wall-normal face velocity over the same run. Test: [`tests/engine/closed-water.test.mjs`](https://github.com/nathansenn/box3d-WEBGPU/blob/main/tests/engine/closed-water.test.mjs), "unforced closed basin conserves mass and bounded modified energy over 24000 ticks".

</details>

### What is not validated: closed-basin water

- Linear waves on a flat bottom: small surface perturbations and wavelengths long relative to depth. No nonlinear advection, breaking, wetting and drying or bathymetry.
- The cases validate the discretisation of the linear equations, not that shallow-water physics describes a given flow. High-frequency input is a stability stress only.
- These rows run the CPU reference. The WebGPU solver is compared with it elsewhere (not in this report) and no speed-up is claimed.
- The other water models of the application (the open absorbing model, GPU water effects) have no rows here.
- No empirical calibration against a tank or a measurement.
